A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VERA research, with matching authors, method, and retained experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection cover the complete documents, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original HarmBench evaluations, transferability and defense experiments, diversity and efficiency measurements, and attacker-backbone and KL ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds optimization controls, judge analyses, AdvBench evaluation, and additional defense experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same variational objective, LoRA attacker, judge approximation, REINFORCE updates, and early stopping. Alternative judges are evaluated within the existing framework; the proposed procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a 50-question AdvBench subset evaluated on LLaMA2-7B-Chat and Vicuna-7B. It also adds LLaMA Guard, SmoothLLM, and RA-LLM defense scenarios beyond the retained Perplexity Filter and Circuit Breaker evaluations, substantially broadening evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 introduces an evaluated frozen-attacker Best-of-N comparator in Table 5. The main HarmBench comparator set is unchanged. The added benchmark and defense comparisons otherwise use attack methods already evaluated in v1, including GCG, AutoDAN, GPTFuzzer, and PAIR.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce substantial new protocols: Best-of-N sampling with N=E×B and no parameter updates, training with three alternative judges, keyword-based scoring on AdvBench, and post-generation defense-bypass evaluation. SmoothLLM uses random character swaps with 10 smoothing copies; RA-LLM uses its stated default threshold. Settings documented for the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing optimization against static sampling, judge-choice sensitivity, and consistency of judge feedback, plus robustness tests against three additional defenses. The existing backbone and KL ablations are retained unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix A.2 to v2 Appendix B.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B newly reports variability across 10 generations per prompt on Vicuna-7B at temperature 0.7, with mean standard deviation 0.107. This is a localized uncertainty analysis absent from v1; it does not establish additional training runs or uncertainty estimates for the retained benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results: VERA versus Best-of-N is 94.0% versus 48.5%; judge-ablation ASRs are 83%, 89%, and 94%. AdvBench yields 16% on LLaMA2 and 86% on Vicuna. Contrary to the accompanying superiority claim, GPTFuzzer reaches 100% on Vicuna in Table 9. New defense results favor VERA on LLaMA Guard, AutoDAN on SmoothLLM, and GCG on RA-LLM.

T1.justification: The posterior formulation, KL/ELBO definitions, and REINFORCE derivation in Equations 1–8 are unchanged. The RLHF comparison is relocated from Appendix A.3/Table 6 to A.2/Table 4 without substantive mathematical revision. No new proof or theoretical result is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: distributional black-box jailbreaking, diverse and fluent prompts, amortized generation, and strong attack, transfer, and defense performance. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of optimization versus system-prompt conditioning, judge calibration and unavoidable proxy bias, and defense-specific behavior under filtering, character swaps, and token deletion. It adds hypotheses about LLaMA Guard training overlap and acknowledges weaker SmoothLLM performance. The original per-behavior training, query-cost, and sparse-reward limitations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 supplies operational details for the added experiments, including the Best-of-N sampling budget, judge identities, AdvBench selection and scoring, and SmoothLLM perturbation configuration. Existing implementation hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are unchanged. v1’s promise to release code upon publication disappears, with no replacement access information in v2.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to RA-LLM, SmoothLLM, StrongREJECT, and Wang et al.’s RL attacker. Section 2 adds a limited contrast concerning the latter’s training overhead and generic exploits. Additional bibliography entries for Chen et al. and LLaMA Guard represent works already cited in v1, rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 adds Section 4.5, acknowledgements, and appendix subheadings; separates ablations into Appendix B; and updates the conference footer. This is limited reorganization rather than extensive rewriting. It also introduces unresolved references, including 'Section ??' in Section 4.1 and 'Table ??' in Appendix B.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the table presentation with dedicated displays for Best-of-N, judge choice, AdvBench, and three additional defenses (Tables 5 and 8–12). Existing main-result tables are enlarged, and appendix tables are relocated and renumbered. Figures 1–5 retain their content, including the diversity and efficiency plots and prompt examples.

improvement.justification: The new optimization control and judge checks address validation gaps in v1, while additional defense results expose useful success and failure conditions. These provide a net improvement in empirical support. The gains are tempered by incompletely specified appendix settings, broken references, and the incorrect AdvBench superiority statement: Table 9 reports VERA at 86% versus GPTFuzzer at 100% on Vicuna. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall improvement.
